evidence: Bottom-set gillnets are by far the greatest threat, in artisanal and industrial fisheries throughout the range. Fishing-related mortality ranges from about 100 (FMA I) to more than 1,000 a year (FMA III), from about 2 to more than 5 times the PBR-based sustainable limit.
where: All FMAs; highest in FMA III

evidence: Occasional captures in coastal and industrial bottom trawls, including the Río de la Plata.
refs: Cappozzo et al. (2007); Franco-Trecu et al. (2019)

evidence: Organochlorines, PBDEs, dechloranes, pyrethroids, UV filters, mercury, cadmium and other trace elements recorded in tissues across the range.
refs: Alonso et al. (2012); Leonel et al. (2010, 2014); Dorneles et al. (2007, 2013)

evidence: Plastic ingestion documented in Argentina and Brazil.
refs: Denuncio et al. (2011); Di Beneditto & Ramos (2014)

evidence: The 2015 Doce River mining dam collapse affected the habitat of the isolated FMA Ia population.
Ports, dredging and vessel traffic in Babitonga Bay; proposed offshore wind farm areas overlap franciscana habitat in southern Brazil.
refs: Paitach et al. (2023); Ribeiro et al. (2026)

threat: Depletion of prey and climate change
evidence: Listed among the other threats in the 2021 synthesis; impacts not quantified.
Historical use of bycaught animals as bait, food or oil (Atafona, Rio Grande do Sul, Paraná, Uruguay; "mushame" in Argentina). No intentional kills reported.
where: FMA Ib; FMA IIb; FMA III; FMA IV
